title: Yash opens up about 'pressure' of playing Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana': 'I have given a different take on it'
summary: Indian star Yash says he felt pressure portraying Ravana in director Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana but insists he has offered a distinct interpretation. Speaking to The Times of India Entertainment Desk, Yash acknowledged expectations around such an iconic character and emphasized his intention to present a fresh, nuanced take that respects the epic while exploring new dimensions of the role.

In a recent conversation with the Times of India Entertainment Desk, actor Yash spoke candidly about the pressure that comes with playing Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's adaptation of the Ramayana. The role, rooted in one of the subcontinent's most enduring epics, carries heavy expectations from audiences and critics alike. Yash acknowledged that portraying such a layered and mythic antagonist brings scrutiny, but said he embraced the challenge. "I have given a different take on it," he told the outlet, emphasizing his aim to bring nuance rather than a one-dimensional portrayal.

Yash described the responsibility of interpreting a legendary figure with sensitivity and originality. While Ravana is often cast strictly as a villain in popular retellings, the actor suggested there is room to explore motivations, complexity and humanity within the character without diminishing the narrative's moral contours. He framed his approach as an attempt to balance fidelity to the epic's core with a fresh perspective that might invite new conversations about the character's place in the story.

Director Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana is being watched closely for its scale and creative choices, and casting decisions like Yash's inclusion have heightened public interest. Industry observers note that reimagining canonical figures is inherently fraught but can also yield compelling cinema when treated thoughtfully. Yash's comments signal an awareness of those risks and a willingness to be judged by audiences when the film reaches them.

The actor expressed gratitude for the trust placed in him by the filmmakers and said he hopes viewers will respond to the depth he sought to bring to Ravana. As conversations build around the adaptation, Yash's remark that he has "given a different take" underscores both the ambition behind the project and the evolving ways filmmakers and actors approach mythological material in contemporary cinema.
